title: Crooked indifferentiability of a permutation-based sponge
summary: Determine whether the source sponge remains crooked-indifferentiable when its random-permutation primitive and distinguisher support inverse queries.

formal_statement.body: Let $P$ be a random permutation and let $widetilde P$ be an admissible subverted implementation in the source crooked-indifferentiability game. For the source-compatible sponge construction using $widetilde P$, prove crooked indifferentiability from a random oracle for every efficient subversion and distinguisher with forward and inverse access under the source query, rate, capacity, and subversion bounds, or exhibit a compatible subversion and distinguisher that separates the construction.

scope.domain: Permutation-based sponge hash constructions under adversarial primitive subversion
assumptions: The construction is the source sponge mode
The ideal primitive is a random permutation
The subverted implementation and distinguisher may make forward and inverse primitive queries
Security is the source crooked-indifferentiability experiment
scope.unresolved_remainder: No inspected later result proves or refutes the complete permutation-sponge crooked-indifferentiability predicate. Ordinary indifferentiability results and crooked Feistel constructions use an honest permutation or a different construction/primitive role and do not cover this remainder.

progress.summary: The source explicitly identifies crooked indifferentiability of a sponge in the random-permutation model as its first natural research problem after the inverse-query obstruction.
